25	        "role": "lower_symmetry",
26	    },
27	    {
28	        "case_label": "public_lower_symmetry_unc",
29	        "topology_name": "unc",
30	        "role": "lower_symmetry",
31	    },
32	    {
33	        "case_label": "public_lower_symmetry_pts",
34	        "topology_name": "pts",
35	        "role": "lower_symmetry",
36	    },
37	    {
38	        "case_label": "public_lower_symmetry_tbo",
39	        "topology_name": "tbo",
40	        "role": "lower_symmetry",
41	    },
42	    {
43	        "case_label": "public_lower_symmetry_sod",
44	        "topology_name": "sod",
45	        "role": "lower_symmetry",
46	    },
47	    {
48	        "case_label": "public_pinned_control_pcu",
49	        "topology_name": "pcu",
50	        "role": "pinned_control",
51	    },
52	]
53	
54	
55	def write_report(payload: dict[str, object], exit_code: int) -> int:
56	    REPORT_PATH.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
57	    text = json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
58	    REPORT_PATH.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
59	    print(text, end="")
60	    return exit_code
61	
62	
63	def max_bond_error(framework) -> float:
64	    graph = framework.graph
65	    cell = np.asarray(graph.graph["cell"], dtype=float)
66	    inverse = np.linalg.inv(cell)
67	    errors: list[float] = []
68	
69	    def target_bond_length(left: int, right: int) -> float:
70	        left_symbol = graph.nodes[left]["symbol"]
71	        right_symbol = graph.nodes[right]["symbol"]
72	        return float(CovalentRadius.radius[left_symbol] + CovalentRadius.radius[right_symbol])
73	
74	    for left, right in graph.edges():
75	        if graph.nodes[left]["slot"] == graph.nodes[right]["slot"]:
76	            continue
77	        delta = np.asarray(graph.nodes[left]["coord"], dtype=float) - np.asarray(
78	            graph.nodes[right]["coord"], dtype=float
79	        )
80	        delta -= np.round(delta @ inverse) @ cell
81	        errors.append(abs(float(np.linalg.norm(delta)) - target_bond_length(left, right)))
82	    if not errors:
83	        raise ValueError("no inter-slot bonds were found in the public case")
84	    return max(errors)
85	
86	
87	def build_public_case(topology_name: str) -> tuple[object, object, float, float]:
88	    sys.path.insert(0, str(SOURCE_ROOT / "src"))
89	    from autografs import Autografs
90	
91	    mofgen = Autografs()
92	    topology = mofgen.topologies[topology_name]
93	    building_units = mofgen.list_building_units(sieve=topology_name)
94	    mappings = {slot_type: options[0] for slot_type, options in building_units.items()}
95	
96	    baseline = mofgen.build(topology, mappings=dict(mappings), max_rmsd=1.0)
97	    relaxed = mofgen.build(
98	        topology,
99	        mappings=dict(mappings),
100	        max_rmsd=1.0,
101	        relax_embedding=True,
102	    )
103	    return baseline, relaxed, max_bond_error(baseline), max_bond_error(relaxed)
104	
105	
106	def main() -> int:
107	    try:
108	        observations: list[dict[str, object]] = []
109	        for case in CASES:
110	            baseline, relaxed, baseline_error, relaxed_error = build_public_case(
111	                case["topology_name"]
112	            )
113	            baseline_volume = float(baseline.structure.volume)
114	            relaxed_volume = float(relaxed.structure.volume)
115	            error_delta = relaxed_error - baseline_error
116	            volume_delta = relaxed_volume - baseline_volume
117	
118	            if not all(
119	                math.isfinite(value)
120	                for value in [
121	                    baseline_error,
122	                    relaxed_error,
123	                    baseline_volume,
124	                    relaxed_volume,
125	                    error_delta,
126	                    volume_delta,
127	                ]
128	            ):
129	                raise ValueError(
130	                    f"non-finite observation produced by the public case {case['case_label']}"
131	                )
132	
133	            record: dict[str, object] = {
134	                "case_label": case["case_label"],
135	                "role": case["role"],
136	                "topology_name": case["topology_name"],
137	                "baseline_max_bond_error": baseline_error,
138	                "relaxed_max_bond_error": relaxed_error,
139	                "bond_error_delta": error_delta,
140	                "closure_budget": CLOSURE_BUDGET,
141	                "within_budget": relaxed_error <= baseline_error + CLOSURE_BUDGET,
142	                "budget_margin": baseline_error + CLOSURE_BUDGET - relaxed_error,
143	                "baseline_volume": baseline_volume,
144	                "relaxed_volume": relaxed_volume,
145	                "volume_delta": volume_delta,
146	                "volume_ratio": relaxed_volume / baseline_volume,
147	                "volume_ratio_limit": CELL_VOLUME_RATIO_LIMIT,
148	                "within_volume_budget": relaxed_volume
149	                <= baseline_volume * CELL_VOLUME_RATIO_LIMIT,
150	            }
151	            if case["role"] == "pinned_control":
152	                record["structure_unchanged"] = bool(
153	                    np.allclose(
154	                        baseline.structure.lattice.matrix,
155	                        relaxed.structure.lattice.matrix,
156	                    )
157	                    and np.allclose(
158	                        baseline.structure.cart_coords,
159	                        relaxed.structure.cart_coords,
160	                    )
161	                )
162	            observations.append(record)
163	
164	        lower_symmetry_ok = all(
165	            bool(record["within_budget"] and record["within_volume_budget"])
166	            for record in observations
167	            if record["role"] == "lower_symmetry"
168	        )
169	        pinned_control = next(
170	            record for record in observations if record["role"] == "pinned_control"
171	        )
172	        pinned_ok = bool(pinned_control["structure_unchanged"])
173	
174	        return write_report(
175	            {
176	                "schema_version": "1.0",
177	                "status": "post_fix_success" if lower_symmetry_ok and pinned_ok else "pre_fix_expected_failure",
178	                "observation": {
179	                    "cases": observations,
180	                    "lower_symmetry_ok": lower_symmetry_ok,
181	                    "pinned_control_ok": pinned_ok,
182	                },
183	            },
184	            0 if lower_symmetry_ok and pinned_ok else 1,
185	        )
186	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
187	        return write_report(
188	            {
189	                "schema_version": "1.0",
190	                "status": "runner_failure",
191	                "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
192	                "error": str(exc),
193	            },
194	            2,
195	        )
196	
197	
198	if __name__ == "__main__":
199	    raise SystemExit(main())
200

1	# AuToGraFS calibrated relaxed embedding
2	
3	AuToGraFS generates framework structures from topological blueprints and
4	building units. The relevant behavior for this task is the optional relaxed
5	embedding workflow, which allows slot positions to move during optimization
6	while preserving the assigned net.
7	
8	The supplied public panel shows that this path can produce geometry that is
9	inconsistent with the ordinary build on several valid lower-symmetry inputs,
10	while a pinned control remains unchanged. The relaxed workflow is not required
11	to beat the ordinary build in every case, but it must stay within the
12	documented closure and volume envelopes.
13	
14	## What the public reproduction checks
15	
16	The public reproduction compares the ordinary build and the relaxed build on a
17	panel of valid inputs and reports the measured geometry.
18	
19	## Relevant public definitions
20	
21	- Lower-symmetry nets may need slot motion to fit real building units.
22	- The relaxed mode is a geometric optimization on the same net.
23	- Fully pinned nets should remain unchanged when relaxation has nothing to
24	  optimize.
25	- The relaxed workflow should stay within the documented closure and volume
26	  budgets on the supplied lower-symmetry cases.
27	- A repaired implementation should keep the relaxed workflow geometrically
28	  consistent across the supplied panel.

1	# AuToGraFS
2	
3	[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/AuToGraFS.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/AuToGraFS/)
4	[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/AuToGraFS.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/AuToGraFS/)
5	[![CI](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
6	[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/DCoupry/autografs/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/DCoupry/autografs)
7	[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/DCoupry/autografs.svg)](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/blob/master/LICENSE.txt)
8	
9	**AuToGraFS** — the *Automatic Topological Generator for Framework Structures* —
10	generates Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs), Covalent Organic Frameworks (COFs)
11	and other periodic framework materials by mapping molecular building blocks
12	(SBUs) onto topological blueprints (nets). It also runs the pipeline in
13	reverse: deconstruct an experimental structure back into building blocks and
14	identify its net.
15	
16	```python
17	from autografs import Autografs
18	
19	mofgen = Autografs()
20	pcu = mofgen.topologies["pcu"]
21	mof = mofgen.build(pcu, mappings={
22	    slot: "Zn_mof5_octahedral" if len(slot.atoms.indices_from_symbol("X")) == 6
23	    else "Benzene_linear"
24	    for slot in pcu.mappings
25	})
26	mof.write_cif("mof5.cif")   # cubic, a = 12.89 A (experiment: 12.9)
27	```
28	
29	Original publication: [*"Automatic Topological Generator for Framework
30	Structures"*](http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/jp507643v),
31	Addicoat, Coupry & Heine, *J. Phys. Chem. A* 2014, 118 (40), 9607.
32	
33	## Why AuToGraFS?
34	
35	Several excellent framework assemblers exist — notably
36	[PORMAKE](https://github.com/Sangwon91/PORMAKE) (Lee *et al.*, whose MIT-licensed
37	building-block library AuToGraFS gratefully bundles) and
38	[ToBaCCo](https://github.com/tobacco-mofs/tobacco_3.0) (Colón / Gómez-Gualdrón
39	groups). AuToGraFS was one of the first tools in this space (2014) and version 3
40	is a ground-up rewrite around a small set of design choices:
41	
42	- **Works out of the box.** `pip install AuToGraFS` ships **2686 RCSR
43	  topologies** and **930 building blocks** (63 curated SBUs + the 867-block
44	  PORMAKE library, 2- to 24-connected). No database generation step, no
45	  external binaries for building. **96.5 % of the shipped topologies are
46	  buildable immediately** (see [library coverage](docs/coverage.md)).
47	- **2D nets are first-class.** The 200 RCSR layer nets (hcb, sql, kgm, ...)
48	  that COF chemistry builds on are stored as plane-group topologies; a build
49	  produces a flat layer, and `Framework.stack()` turns it into a bulk crystal
50	  with AA / AB / serrated / staggered stacking at a chosen interlayer spacing.
51	- **Geometry, not symmetry tables.** SBUs are matched to slots by optimally
52	  rotating their connection vectors onto the slot's (Hungarian assignment +
53	  Kabsch, *proper rotations only* — chiral building blocks are never silently
54	  mirrored). Point-group labels are metadata, not gates, so low-symmetry (C1)
55	  vertices stay usable.
56	- **Physically meaningful cells.** The cell is optimized so that every
57	  inter-SBU bond sits at its covalent (Cordero) bond length, with the crystal
58	  system's constraints enforced (a cubic net optimizes a single length).
59	  MOF-5 comes out cubic at 12.89 Å against the experimental 12.9 — *before*
60	  any force-field relaxation.
61	- **Fails loudly, never silently.** Optional hard gates (`max_rmsd`,
62	  `min_distance`) raise typed exceptions instead of returning distorted or
63	  interpenetrating structures. Identical inputs give identical outputs.
64	- **Runs in reverse.** Deconstruct a CIF (MOF or COF) into library-ready SBUs
65	  and identify its net; harvest a whole SBU library from a folder of
66	  structures.
67	- **Rod MOFs, both directions.** The MOF-74 family and other rod MOFs are built
68	  around an *infinite* 1-periodic metal-oxo chain — no finite building block.
69	  AuToGraFS deconstructs them, gives each rod a screw-aware canonical identity
70	  (helicity is chiral and preserved), and **builds them forward again** — for
71	  straight *and* helical rods, including general (non-180°) screws. See
72	  [Rod MOFs](docs/rods.md).
73	- **Post-processing built in.** UFF4MOF assignment on every output, GULP input
74	  generation, EQeq partial charges, and one-call relaxation — in-process
75	  LAMMPS/UFF4MOF or any ASE calculator (GFN-FF, GFN1-xTB, DFTB+) — plus elastic
76	  constants via finite differences (`pip install "autografs[relax]"`).
77	- **Safe, versioned data formats.** Topology libraries are plain JSON
78	  (diffable, shareable, survives pymatgen upgrades) — not pickles.
79	- **A guided CLI.** The `autografs` wizard walks through
80	  topology → SBUs → build → stack → export without writing a script.
81	- **MIT licensed**, pure-Python installation on Linux / macOS / Windows.
82	
83	If you need features AuToGraFS doesn't have yet (see [Roadmap](#roadmap)),
84	PORMAKE and ToBaCCo are actively maintained and may fit better — comparisons
85	age quickly, so evaluate against their current versions.
86	
87	## Installation
88	
89	```bash
90	pip install AuToGraFS
91	```
92	
93	Requires Python ≥ 3.11. Core dependencies: pymatgen, ASE, numpy, scipy,
94	networkx.
95	
96	Optional extras:
97	
98	```bash
99	pip install "autografs[relax]"   # UFF4MOF relaxation via LAMMPS
100	```
101	
102	On Windows, the LAMMPS wheel additionally needs the Microsoft MPI runtime
103	(`winget install Microsoft.MSMPI`).
104	
105	Development install:
106	
107	```bash
108	git clone https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs.git
109	cd autografs
110	pip install -e ".[dev]"
111	```
112	
113	## Quickstart: MOF-5
114	
115	```python
116	from autografs import Autografs
117	
118	mofgen = Autografs()
119	
120	# what fits the pcu net?
121	available = mofgen.list_building_units(sieve="pcu")
122	for slot_type, sbu_names in available.items():
123	    print(slot_type, len(sbu_names), "candidates")
124	# Oh 6 : ... candidates      (the octahedral node)
125	# D*h 2 : ... candidates     (the linear edge)
126	
127	# pick one SBU per slot type
128	topology = mofgen.topologies["pcu"]
129	mappings = {}
130	for slot_type in topology.mappings:
131	    n_connections = len(slot_type.atoms.indices_from_symbol("X"))
132	    if n_connections == 6:
133	        mappings[slot_type] = "Zn_mof5_octahedral"
134	    else:
135	        mappings[slot_type] = "Benzene_linear"
136	
137	mof = mofgen.build(topology, mappings=mappings)
138	print(mof)
139	# Framework('pcu', 'Zn4 H12 C24 O13', abc=(12.89, 12.89, 12.89))
140	
141	mof.write_cif("mof5.cif")
142	```
143	
144	Then keep going: [build options and batch enumeration](docs/building.md),
145	[2D COFs](docs/cofs-and-stacking.md), [editing](docs/editing.md), or
146	[deconstruction](docs/deconstruction.md).
147	
148	## Command line
149	
150	No script needed — the `autografs` wizard covers build, deconstruct, stack, and
151	export interactively, and `autografs-topologies` (re)builds a topology library:
152	
153	```bash
154	autografs                                    # bundled libraries; guided session
155	autografs --xyz my_sbus.xyz                  # add custom building blocks
156	autografs-topologies --use_rcsr -o topologies.json.gz   # regenerate the library
157	```
158	
159	Full walkthrough of both commands: [Command line](docs/cli.md).
160	
161	## Documentation
162	
163	The README is the overview; the depth lives in `docs/`:
164	
165	- **[Building frameworks](docs/building.md)** — the Python API: exploring the
166	  libraries, `build`, `build_all`, working with the `Framework` result
167	  (porosity, save/load, exports), relaxation (LAMMPS or any ASE calculator),
168	  partial charges, elastic constants, error handling.
169	- **[2D COFs and stacking](docs/cofs-and-stacking.md)** — layer nets, turning a
170	  layer into a bulk crystal (AA / AB / serrated / staggered), and commensurate
171	  twisted (moiré) bilayers.
172	- **[Rod MOFs](docs/rods.md)** — 1-periodic building units (MOF-74 & friends):
173	  deconstructing, screw-aware canonical identity, and forward building of
174	  straight and helical rods.
175	- **[Editing](docs/editing.md)** — editing SBUs before a build, and post-build
176	  supercells, statistical defects, and functionalization.
177	- **[Deconstruction](docs/deconstruction.md)** — CIF → SBUs + net, net
178	  identification, interpenetration, COFs, batch harvesting, and assembly
179	  fingerprints.
180	- **[Command line](docs/cli.md)** — the `autografs` wizard and
181	  `autografs-topologies` in full.
182	- **[Extending the libraries](docs/extending.md)** — custom SBUs (XYZ) and
183	  custom topologies (CGD → JSON).
184	- **[How it works & architecture](docs/internals.md)** — the 2014 idea, the
185	  build pipeline, and a module map of the codebase.
186	- **[Library coverage](docs/coverage.md)** — what fraction of RCSR is buildable
187	  today, and the nets that aren't.
188	
189	## FAQ
190	
191	**Does it build COFs?** Yes — 2D layer nets are first-class. Build a flat layer
192	on a layer net (hcb, sql, ...), then `Framework.stack()` turns it into a bulk
193	crystal. See [2D COFs and stacking](docs/cofs-and-stacking.md).
194	
195	**Do I need LAMMPS?** Only for `Framework.relax()`. Building, export,
196	deconstruction, and everything else are pure-Python. Install the relaxation
197	backend with `pip install "autografs[relax]"`.
198	
199	**My SBU is rejected / I get `AlignmentError` — why?** The build gate is
200	geometric: the SBU's connection-vector *shape* doesn't match the slot's within
201	`max_rmsd`. Raise `max_rmsd`, pick a net whose vertex figure fits, or edit the
202	SBU. Point-group symmetry is diagnostic metadata, not the gate.
203	
204	**Is my net in the library?** 2686 RCSR nets ship; list them with
205	`mofgen.list_topologies()`. 96.5 % are buildable out of the box — the rest, and
206	how to enable them, are in [library coverage](docs/coverage.md).
207	
208	**Does it handle rod MOFs (MOF-74, metal carboxylates)?** Yes — rod MOFs, whose
209	building unit is an infinite 1-periodic chain, are a first-class case in both
210	directions: deconstruct them, harvest rod families with a screw-aware canonical
211	identity, and build them forward (straight *and* helical rods, including general
212	non-180° screws). See [Rod MOFs](docs/rods.md).
213	
214	**`deconstruct()` raised `DeconstructionError` — why?** It refuses disordered
215	structures, molecular crystals (no periodic framework to analyze), *bare*
216	1-periodic polymers with no framework connections, and 2-periodic (layer)
217	building units. Rod MOFs and metal-free COFs *are* supported. See
218	[Deconstruction](docs/deconstruction.md).
219	
220	**CIF or JSON — which should I save?** CIF for downstream tools, but it loses
221	the bond graph and per-atom provenance that post-build editing needs. Use
222	`Framework.save()` / `Framework.load()` (versioned JSON) to keep a framework
223	editable across sessions.
224	
225	**Can I still load my old `.pkl` topology library?** Yes, with a warning.
226	Convert it once with `autografs.topology_io.save_topologies` to the JSON format
227	and keep that.
228	
229	## Development
230	
231	```bash
232	pip install -e ".[dev]"
233	
234	pytest                    # slow tests auto-skipped
235	pytest -m slow            # only the slow tests
236	ruff check src tests      # lint
237	ruff format src tests     # format
238	mypy src/autografs        # type check
239	```
240	
241	Tests live in `tests/`; `scripts/` holds the coverage audit
242	(`sbu_coverage.py`), the PORMAKE import (`import_pormake_bbs.py`), and fixture
243	generators. Architecture and module map: [How it works](docs/internals.md).
244	
245	## Roadmap
246	
247	The 3.x line has reached feature parity with 2.x and gone well beyond it: the
248	inverse pipeline (deconstruction, net identification, SBU harvesting for MOFs
249	and COFs), rod-MOF support in both directions (including helical rods), IZA

1	# Building frameworks (Python API)
2	
3	*Part of the [AuToGraFS documentation](../README.md#documentation).*
4	
5	For the mechanics behind these calls — the sieve, alignment, and cell
6	optimization — see [How it works](internals.md).
7	
8	## Exploring the libraries
9	
10	```python
11	from autografs import Autografs
12	
13	mofgen = Autografs()
14	
15	mofgen.list_topologies()                        # all RCSR symbols
16	mofgen.list_topologies(sieve="Benzene_linear")  # nets this SBU fits
17	
18	# building units compatible with a net, grouped by slot type;
19	# slot types with no compatible SBU are absent from the dict
20	mofgen.list_building_units(sieve="srs")
21	
22	# raw access
23	sbu = mofgen.sbu["Zn_mof5_octahedral"]          # a Fragment
24	topology = mofgen.topologies["tbo"]             # a Topology (lazy library)
25	zeolite = mofgen.topologies["FAU"]              # IZA framework codes work too
26	
27	print(len(topology))                  # number of slots
28	print(topology.cell.abc)              # blueprint cell
29	print(topology.spacegroup_number)     # 225
30	print(topology.is_2d)                 # False
31	for slot_type, indices in topology.mappings.items():
32	    print(slot_type, "fills slots", indices)
33	```
34	
35	55 IZA zeolite framework type codes (FAU, LTA, CHA, SOD, RHO, ...) resolve
36	as lookup-only aliases onto the RCSR nets that carry them in lowercase —
37	`mofgen.topologies["FAU"]` and `mofgen.topologies["fau"]` are the same
38	entry, and enumeration (`build_all`, coverage counts) never sees a net
39	twice. The mapping ships in `data/iza_aliases.json` (regenerate with
40	`scripts/make_iza_aliases.py`); `mofgen.topologies.aliases` lists it.
41	
42	## Building
43	
44	`build` takes a topology and a mapping from slot types (or explicit slot
45	indices) to SBUs, given as library names or `Fragment` objects:
46	
47	```python
48	mof = mofgen.build(
49	    topology,
50	    mappings={node_type: "Zn_mof5_octahedral", edge_type: "Benzene_linear"},
51	    refine_cell=True,   # optimize cell parameters (default)
52	    max_rmsd=0.3,       # reject builds with bad shape matches
53	    min_distance=1.0,   # reject builds with overlapping atoms
54	)
55	```
56	
57	- **`max_rmsd`** gates the *directional* mismatch between an SBU's connection
58	  vectors and its slot's (dimensionless; 0 is a perfect shape match).
59	  Incompatible geometry raises `autografs.AlignmentError` instead of returning
60	  a distorted structure.
61	- **`min_distance`** screens the built structure: if any two non-bonded atoms
62	  (all periodic images included) are closer than this many Å,
63	  `autografs.OverlapError` is raised instead of returning overlapping or
64	  interpenetrating output. The same check is available on any result as
65	  `Framework.min_contact()`.
66	- **Slot indices** (integers) may be used as mapping keys to place a specific
67	  SBU on a specific slot, overriding the slot-type choice:
68	
69	```python
70	mappings = {node_type: "sbu_A", edge_type: "linker_1", 7: "linker_2"}
71	```
72	
73	### Embedding relaxation
74	
75	A build normally places every SBU at its blueprint slot centre and varies only
76	the cell's free parameters, so the *proportions* of the structure are whatever
77	the net's idealized (maximum-symmetry, near-equal-edge) embedding chose. For
78	high-symmetry nets those are exact by symmetry — pcu, dia, fcu and friends
79	have nothing to choose — but lower-symmetry nets inherit proportions that can
80	be measurably wrong for real chemistry: no single cell parameter can give a
81	long linker and a short one each the room they need.
82	
83	```python
84	mof = mofgen.build(topology, mappings, relax_embedding=True)
85	```
86	
87	frees the slot centres as extra optimization degrees of freedom while
88	preserving the declared symmetry of the net. Fully pinned nets (their
89	embedding is already exact by symmetry) have nothing to relax and build
90	exactly as without the flag; for the rest, the topology of the output is
91	unchanged (`verify_net` applies as usual) while the packing follows the SBUs
92	instead of the idealization. Off by default; the geometry of default builds
93	is unchanged.
94	
95	## Batch enumeration
96	
97	`build_all` attempts every compatible SBU combination on every (or a subset
98	of) topology:
99	
100	```python
101	frameworks = mofgen.build_all(
102	    topology_subset=["pcu", "dia", "srs"],
103	    sbu_subset=None,          # default: whole SBU library
104	    max_rmsd=0.3,
105	    min_distance=1.0,
106	    max_per_topology=50,      # cap the combinatorial explosion...
107	    seed=42,                  # ...with a reproducible random sample
108	    n_jobs=4,                 # parallel builds (near-linear speedup)
109	)
110	```
111	
112	Failed builds are counted and skipped, not raised. Multinodal nets have
113	combinatorially many SBU choices; when the full product exceeds
114	`max_per_topology`, a seeded sample of distinct combinations is built instead.
115	Passing `max_per_topology=-1` (or `None`, the default) disables the cap and
116	enumerates exhaustively. Either way the total combination count over all
117	buildable topologies is logged before the first build starts, so an
118	exhaustive run can be cost-estimated — and aborted — while still cheap.
119	
120	Long runs can checkpoint: with `checkpoint_dir="ckpt/"` every finished
121	combination is recorded on disk atomically (built frameworks as `.json.gz`,
122	gate rejections as `.failed` markers), and rerunning with the same arguments
123	and the same directory skips them, reloading their outcomes instead of
124	rebuilding — an interrupted enumeration resumes where it stopped. The ledger
125	records outcomes, not settings, so rerun with the same gates and seed.
126	
127	## Working with the result
128	
129	`build` returns a `Framework`:
130	
131	```python
132	mof.structure          # pymatgen Structure (wrapped; site props: tags, ufftype)
133	mof.graph              # networkx bond graph: symbols, coords, UFF4MOF
134	                       # atom types, bond orders, tags (source of truth)
135	mof.formula            # 'Zn4 H12 C24 O13'
136	mof.lattice            # pymatgen Lattice
137	mof.bonds              # [(i, j, bond_order), ...]
138	mof.mmtypes            # UFF4MOF atom types, node order
139	mof.min_contact()      # closest non-bonded contact (all images)
140	mof.slots              # {slot index: SBU name} for every placed unit
141	
142	mof.density                     # g/cm3 (MOF-5: ~0.6)
143	mof.void_fraction()             # geometric; probe_radius=1.2 for a He probe
144	mof.largest_cavity_diameter()   # LCD, Angstrom (MOF-5: ~15)
145	mof.pore_limiting_diameter()    # PLD, Angstrom (MOF-5: ~8) - the channel bottleneck
146	
147	mof.write_cif("out.cif", symprec=None)   # symprec symmetrizes if set
148	atoms = mof.to_ase()                     # periodic ase.Atoms
149	mof.view()                               # ASE viewer
150	gulp_input = mof.to_gulp()               # UFF4MOF optimization input for GULP
151	```
152	
153	CIF export is for downstream tools; it loses the bond graph and the
154	per-atom provenance that post-build editing needs. To keep a framework
155	editable across sessions, save it to the versioned JSON format instead:
156	
157	```python
158	mof.save("mof5.json.gz")                 # bond graph, tags, provenance, energy
159	mof = Framework.load("mof5.json.gz")     # editable exactly like the original
160	defective = mof.supercell(2).defects(fraction=0.1, seed=42)
161	```
162	
163	See [Editing](editing.md) for supercells, defects, and functionalization.
164	
165	## UFF4MOF relaxation
166	
167	`relax` optimizes the geometry and cell with the UFF4MOF force field through
168	LAMMPS, in-process, and returns a new `Framework` with the same bond graph:
169	
170	```bash
171	pip install "autografs[relax]"
172	```
173	
174	```python
175	relaxed = mof.relax()          # UFF4MOF, alternating cell + FIRE
176	relaxed.energy                 # kcal/mol per unit cell
177	relaxed.write_cif("relaxed.cif")
178	```
179	
180	Cells smaller than the non-bonded cutoff (12.5 Å by default) are relaxed as an
181	internal supercell and folded back transparently. `"UFF"` and `"Dreiding"` are
182	also accepted as `force_field`.
183	
184	### Higher levels: any ASE calculator
185	
186	Passing `calculator` switches `relax` to a thin ASE bridge — the higher rungs
187	of a multi-fidelity funnel. Use a name or any ASE calculator instance:
188	
189	```python
190	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator="gfn-ff")   # periodic GFN-FF (xtb-python)
191	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator="gfn1")     # GFN1-xTB (pip install tblite)
192	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator="dftb")     # DFTB+ (binary + SK files)
193	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator=my_ase_calculator, fmax=0.01, steps=1000)
194	```
195	
196	The bond graph is preserved exactly as on the LAMMPS path, energies land in
197	`Framework.energy` in the same kcal/mol-per-cell convention, and
198	`relax_cell=False` keeps the cell fixed (cell relaxation needs a calculator
199	that provides stress). `"gfn2"` is rejected up front: GFN2-xTB has no
200	periodic implementation.
201	
202	## Partial charges
203	
204	`assign_charges` puts per-atom point charges on the bond graph — the input
205	GCMC adsorption codes need. The built-in scheme is EQeq (extended charge
206	equilibration, Wilmer et al. 2012): periodic, parameter-free beyond two
207	published dials, no DFT required, one linear solve. The implementation is a
208	numpy port validated against the reference C++ code:
209	
210	```python
211	charged = mof.assign_charges("eqeq")   # returns a new Framework
212	charged.charges                        # per-atom array, sums to 0
213	charged.write_cif("charged.cif")       # gains _atom_site_charge (RASPA-style)
214	charged.to_ase()                       # charges become ASE initial charges
215	charged.save("charged.json.gz")        # charges survive save/load and editing
216	```
217	
218	Other schemes (DDEC from DFT output, ML charge models) plug in through a
219	registry:
220	
221	```python
222	from autografs.charges import register_charge_method
223	
224	@register_charge_method("mymodel")
225	def my_charges(framework, **options):
226	    return model.predict(framework)    # one charge per atom, node order
227	
228	charged = mof.assign_charges("mymodel")
229	```
230	
231	Treat the scheme as a controlled variable in any adsorption study — EQeq and
232	DDEC charges differ systematically, and uptake predictions inherit that
233	difference.
234	
235	## Elastic constants
236	
237	`elastic_properties` computes the 6×6 stiffness tensor at the same force-field
238	level (same optional install), by central finite differences of the LAMMPS
239	stress under the six Voigt strains after a full relaxation — the protocol of
240	the LAMMPS `ELASTIC` example, run in-process:
241	
242	```python
243	props = mof.elastic_properties()   # relaxes first; UFF4MOF by default
244	props.stiffness                    # 6x6 Voigt matrix, GPa, symmetrized
245	props.bulk_hill, props.shear_hill  # Voigt/Reuss/Hill averages
246	props.young_hill, props.poisson_hill
247	props.young_min, props.young_max   # directional extrema (anisotropy)
248	props.young_modulus([1, 1, 0])     # along a specific direction
249	props.is_stable                    # Born stability (positive definite)
250	```
251	
252	The tensor is projected onto the framework's crystal system (averaged over its
253	point-group rotations), so a cubic framework reports the exact 3-constant
254	cubic pattern. Note that the detected symmetry is that of the *built model*,
255	which can be lower than the net's: MOF-5 built on **pcu** keeps each benzene
256	ring in a fixed plane and comes out orthorhombic (real MOF-5 is cubic only
257	through ring disorder). Treat the numbers as screening-level: UFF4MOF
258	stiffnesses carry force-field error; rankings across candidates are the
259	reliable output. For 2D layer frameworks only the in-plane components are
260	physical — the padded c axis is not.
261	
262	## Error handling
263	
264	All library exceptions derive from `autografs.AutografsError`:
265	
266	```python
267	from autografs import AlignmentError, OverlapError
268	from autografs.exceptions import StackingError, RelaxationError
269	
270	try:
271	    mof = mofgen.build(topology, mappings, max_rmsd=0.3, min_distance=1.0)
272	except AlignmentError:   # shape mismatch beyond the gate
273	    ...
274	except OverlapError:     # non-bonded contact below the gate
275	    ...
276	```
277

2	Builder module for AuToGraFS framework generation.
3	
4	This module contains the main Autografs class responsible for generating
5	Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) and other periodic crystalline structures
6	from topological blueprints and Secondary Building Units (SBUs).
7	
8	Classes
9	-------
10	Autografs
11	    Main framework maker class for generating structures.
12	
13	Functions
14	---------
15	build_framework
16	    Library-independent build core, usable from worker processes.
17	
18	Examples
19	--------
20	>>> from autografs.builder import Autografs
21	>>> mofgen = Autografs()
22	>>> topology = mofgen.topologies["pcu"]
23	>>> mappings = mofgen.list_building_units(sieve="pcu")
24	>>> graph = mofgen.build(topology, mappings={k: v[0] for k, v in mappings.items()})
25	"""

66	# Constants for cell parameter optimization
67	NELDER_MEAD_XATOL = 0.1  # Absolute tolerance for cell parameter convergence
68	NELDER_MEAD_FATOL = 0.01  # Absolute tolerance for RMSE convergence
69	# Iteration budget PER FREE CELL PARAMETER: cubic optimizes a single
70	# length, triclinic six parameters - a flat budget starved the latter
71	NELDER_MEAD_MAXITER = 100

74	def build_framework(
75	    topology: Topology,
76	    mappings: dict[int, Fragment],
77	    refine_cell: bool = True,
78	    verbose: bool = False,
79	    max_rmsd: float | None = None,
80	    min_distance: float | None = None,
81	    verify_net: bool = False,
82	    relax_embedding: bool = False,
83	) -> Framework:
84	    """Build one framework from validated slot-index mappings.
85	
86	    This is the library-independent core of Autografs.build(): it
87	    needs no SBU or topology library, only a topology and one private
88	    Fragment per slot index, which also makes it usable from worker
89	    processes. Most callers want Autografs.build(), which resolves
90	    names and slot types first.
91	
92	    Parameters
93	    ----------
94	    topology : Topology
95	        The blueprint; not modified.
96	    mappings : dict[int, Fragment]
97	        One (private) Fragment per slot index, as produced by
98	        Autografs._validate_mappings.
99	    refine_cell : bool, optional
100	        Optimize the crystal system's free cell parameters.
101	    verbose : bool, optional
102	        Log alignment details.
103	    max_rmsd : float or None, optional
104	        Directional shape-mismatch gate; see Autografs.build.
105	    min_distance : float or None, optional
106	        Post-build overlap gate; see Autografs.build.
107	    verify_net : bool, optional
108	        Topological gate; see Autografs.build.
109	    relax_embedding : bool, optional
110	        Add the blueprint's slot displacements to the optimization
111	        problem; see Autografs.build.
112	
113	    Returns
114	    -------
115	    Framework
116	        The built framework.
117	    """
118	    t0 = time.time()
119	    plan = autografs.alignment.prepare_build(
120	        topology, mappings, relax_embedding=relax_embedding
121	    )
122	    x0 = plan.initial_parameters()
123	    if refine_cell and plan.has_pairs:
124	        # Nelder-Mead on the packed parameter vector; the objective is
125	        # pure numpy, no object copies per evaluation.
126	        n_free = plan.cell_param.n_free + plan.n_slot_free
127	        result = minimize(
128	            plan.residual,
129	            x0,
130	            method="Nelder-Mead",
131	            options={
132	                "xatol": NELDER_MEAD_XATOL,
133	                "fatol": NELDER_MEAD_FATOL,
134	                "maxiter": NELDER_MEAD_MAXITER * n_free,
135	            },
136	        )
137	        best_parameters = result.x
138	    else:
139	        if verbose:
140	            logger.info("\t[x] No cell refinement performed.")
141	        best_parameters = x0
142	    best_alignment, lattice, slot_rmsds = plan.finalize(best_parameters)
143	    if max_rmsd is not None:
144	        bad_slots = {i: r for i, r in slot_rmsds.items() if r > max_rmsd}
145	        if bad_slots:
146	            worst = max(bad_slots.values())
147	            raise AlignmentError(
148	                f"{len(bad_slots)} of {len(slot_rmsds)} slots exceed "
149	                f"max_rmsd={max_rmsd:.3f} (worst: {worst:.3f}) "
150	                f"on topology {topology.name}: {sorted(bad_slots)}"
151	            )
152	    if verbose:
153	        a, b, c = lattice.abc
154	        alpha, beta, gamma = lattice.angles
155	        logger.info("\t[x] Best cell parameters:")
156	        logger.info(f"\t\ta={a:<.2f} b={b:<.2f} c={c:<.2f}")
157	        logger.info(f"\t\talpha={alpha:<.1f} beta={beta:<.1f} gamma={gamma:<.1f}")
158	        logger.info(
159	            f"\t[x] Aligned {len(best_alignment)} fragments in {time.time() - t0:.1f} seconds"
160	        )
161	    graph = autografs.utils.fragments_to_networkx(
162	        best_alignment, cell=lattice.matrix, slots=sorted(mappings)
163	    )
164	    framework = Framework(graph, name=topology.name)
165	    if min_distance is not None:
166	        contact = framework.min_contact(cutoff=min_distance)
167	        if contact < min_distance:
168	            raise OverlapError(
169	                f"Closest non-bonded contact is {contact:.2f} A, below "
170	                f"min_distance={min_distance:.2f} A, on topology "
171	                f"{topology.name}: overlapping or interpenetrating output."
172	            )
173	    if verify_net:
174	        framework.verify_net(topology)
175	    return framework

183	def _build_one(
184	    topology: Topology,
185	    mappings: dict[int, Fragment],
186	    refine_cell: bool,
187	    max_rmsd: float | None,
188	    min_distance: float | None,
189	) -> Framework | None:
190	    """Worker-safe build: expected failures become None, not raises."""
191	    try:
192	        return build_framework(
193	            topology,
194	            mappings,
195	            refine_cell=refine_cell,
196	            max_rmsd=max_rmsd,
197	            min_distance=min_distance,
198	        )
199	    except (AlignmentError, OverlapError):
200	        # the quality gates rejecting a combination is the expected
201	        # outcome of an enumeration sweep; nothing to report
202	        return None
203	    except (AssertionError, ValueError):
204	        # unexpected failure types: still skip the combination (a sweep
205	        # must not abort), but leave a diagnosable trace instead of
206	        # only inflating the error-rate statistic
207	        logger.debug(f"Unexpected failure building on {topology.name!r}", exc_info=True)
208	        return None

211	def _build_chunk(
212	    args: tuple[Topology, list[dict[int, Fragment]], bool, float | None, float | None],
213	) -> list[Framework | None]:
214	    """Build several combinations against one shared topology pickle."""
215	    topology, chunk, refine_cell, max_rmsd, min_distance = args
216	    return [
217	        _build_one(topology, mappings, refine_cell, max_rmsd, min_distance)
218	        for mappings in chunk
219	    ]

222	def _batched(iterable: Iterable, size: int):
223	    """Consecutive lists of up to ``size`` items (itertools.batched is
224	    3.12+ and the runtime floor is 3.11)."""
225	    iterator = iter(iterable)
226	    while chunk := list(itertools.islice(iterator, size)):
227	        yield chunk

230	def _deduplicate_frameworks(frameworks: list[Framework]) -> list[Framework]:
231	    """Keep the first representative of each equivalence class.
232	
233	    Structures are pre-binned by reduced formula (different formulas
234	    can never match), then compared within a bin with pymatgen's
235	    StructureMatcher at its default tolerances. First occurrence wins,
236	    so the result order is a stable subsequence of the input.
237	    """
238	    from pymatgen.analysis.structure_matcher import StructureMatcher
239	
240	    matcher = StructureMatcher()
241	    kept: list[Framework] = []
242	    kept_by_formula: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
243	    for framework in frameworks:
244	        formula = framework.structure.composition.reduced_formula
245	        indices = kept_by_formula.setdefault(formula, [])
246	        if any(
247	            matcher.fit(kept[index].structure, framework.structure) for index in indices
248	        ):
249	            continue
250	        indices.append(len(kept))
251	        kept.append(framework)
252	    if len(kept) < len(frameworks):
253	        logger.info(
254	            f"\t[x] Removed {len(frameworks) - len(kept)} structurally "
255	            "equivalent duplicates."
256	        )
257	    return kept

260	def _iter_combinations(
261	    options: list[list[str]],
262	    max_count: int | None,
263	    rng: np.random.Generator,
264	):
265	    """Yield SBU-name combinations: all of them, or a seeded sample.
266	
267	    When the full product exceeds max_count, distinct index tuples are
268	    drawn from the seeded generator (deterministic for a given seed)
269	    and yielded in sorted order.
270	    """
271	    total = math.prod(len(choices) for choices in options)
272	    if max_count is None or total <= max_count:
273	        yield from itertools.product(*options)
274	        return
275	    picks: set[tuple[int, ...]] = set()
276	    attempts = 0
277	    limit = 20 * max_count
278	    while len(picks) < max_count and attempts < limit:
279	        picks.add(tuple(int(rng.integers(len(choices))) for choices in options))
280	        attempts += 1
281	    for pick in sorted(picks):
282	        yield tuple(options[i][j] for i, j in enumerate(pick))

285	class _Checkpoint:
286	    """On-disk ledger of finished build_all combinations.
287	
288	    One entry per (topology, SBU-choice) combination, keyed by a
289	    digest of the names: ``<digest>.json.gz`` holds the built
290	    framework, ``<digest>.failed`` marks a gate rejection. Writes go
291	    through a temp file and an atomic replace, so a killed run never
292	    leaves a truncated entry; a rerun pointed at the same directory
293	    skips finished combinations and reloads their outcomes. The ledger
294	    records outcomes only, not build settings - reruns must use the
295	    same gates and seed for the restored results to mean anything.
296	    """
297	
298	    def __init__(self, directory: str | Path) -> None:
299	        self.directory = Path(directory)
300	        self.directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
301	        self._entries: dict[str, Path] = {}
302	        for path in self.directory.iterdir():
303	            # a .tmp piece is a write that never committed: ignore it,
304	            # the combination will simply be rebuilt
305	            if ".tmp" in path.suffixes:
306	                continue
307	            if path.name.endswith((".json.gz", ".failed")):
308	                self._entries[path.name.split(".", 1)[0]] = path
309	
310	    @staticmethod
311	    def key(topology_name: str, choice: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
312	        """Deterministic filename-safe digest of one combination."""
313	        payload = json.dumps([topology_name, *choice])
314	        return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()
315	
316	    def completed(self, key: str) -> bool:
317	        return key in self._entries
318	
319	    def load(self, key: str) -> Framework | None:
320	        """Recorded outcome: the framework, or None for a rejection."""
321	        path = self._entries[key]
322	        if path.name.endswith(".failed"):
323	            return None
324	        return Framework.load(path)
325	
326	    def record(self, key: str, framework: Framework | None) -> None:
327	        name = f"{key}.json.gz" if framework is not None else f"{key}.failed"
328	        final = self.directory / name
329	        # the temp name keeps the real extension last so Framework.save
330	        # still picks gzip, while '.tmp' marks it uncommitted
331	        tmp = self.directory / f"{key}.tmp.{name.split('.', 1)[1]}"
332	        if framework is None:
333	            tmp.touch()
334	        else:
335	            framework.save(tmp)
336	        tmp.replace(final)
337	        self._entries[key] = final

340	class Autografs:
341	    """Framework maker class to generate periodic structures from topologies.
342	
343	    AuToGraFS: Automatic Topological Generator for Framework Structures.
344	
345	    This class manages libraries of Secondary Building Units (SBUs) and
346	    topological blueprints, providing methods to combine them into
347	    periodic framework structures.
348	
349	    Attributes
350	    ----------
351	    topologies : dict[str, Topology]
352	        Dictionary of available topology blueprints, keyed by name.
353	    sbu : dict[str, Fragment]
354	        Dictionary of available Secondary Building Units, keyed by name.
355	
356	    References
357	    ----------
358	    .. [1] Addicoat, M., Coupry, D. E., & Heine, T. (2014).
359	           The Journal of Physical Chemistry A, 118(40), 9607-14.
360	
361	    Examples
362	    --------
363	    >>> mofgen = Autografs()
364	    >>> print(len(mofgen.topologies))  # Available topologies
365	    >>> print(len(mofgen.sbu))  # Available building units
366	    """
367	
368	    def __init__(
369	        self,
370	        xyzfile: str | None = None,
371	        topofile: str | None = None,
372	    ) -> None:
373	        """Initialize the Autografs framework generator.
374	
375	        Parameters
376	        ----------
377	        xyzfile : str or None, optional
378	            Path to an XYZ file containing custom Secondary Building Units.
379	            If provided, these SBUs will be added to the default library.
380	        topofile : str or None, optional
381	            Path to a pickle file containing custom topologies.
382	            If None, uses the default RCSR topology library.
383	
384	        Examples
385	        --------
386	        >>> mofgen = Autografs()  # Use defaults
387	        >>> mofgen = Autografs(xyzfile="my_sbus.xyz")  # Add custom SBUs
388	        """
389	        super().__init__()
390	        # Initialize instance attributes to avoid sharing between instances
391	        self.topologies: Mapping[str, Topology] = {}
392	        self.sbu: dict[str, Fragment] = {}
393	        logger.info(f"{'*':*^78}")
394	        logger.info(f"*{'AuToGraFS':^76}*")
395	        logger.info(
396	            f"*{'Automatic Topological Generator for Framework Structures':^76}*"
397	        )
398	        logger.info(f"*{'Addicoat, M., Coupry, D. E., & Heine, T. (2014)':^76}*")
399	        logger.info(f"*{'The Journal of Physical Chemistry A, 118(40), 9607-14':^76}*")
400	        logger.info(f"{'*':*^78}")
401	        logger.info("")
402	        logger.info("Setting up libraries...")
403	        self._setup_sbu(xyzfile=xyzfile)
404	        self._setup_topologies(topofile=topofile)
405	        logger.info("")
406	
407	    def build_all(
408	        self,
409	        sbu_subset: list[str] | None = None,
410	        topology_subset: list[str] | None = None,
411	        refine_cell: bool = True,
412	        max_rmsd: float | None = None,
413	        min_distance: float | None = None,
414	        max_per_topology: int | None = None,
415	        seed: int | None = None,
416	        n_jobs: int = 1,
417	        deduplicate: bool = False,
418	        checkpoint_dir: str | Path | None = None,
419	    ) -> list[Framework]:
420	        """
421	        Builds all available structures based on the SBU and Topologies libraries
422	
423	        Parameters
424	        ----------
425	        sbu_subset : list[str] | None, optional
426	            The subset of SBU to build on, by default None
427	        topology_subset : list[str] | None, optional
428	            the subset of topologies to build on, by default None
429	        refine_cell : bool, optional
430	            If True, optimizes cell parameters for each build, by default True
431	        max_rmsd : float or None, optional
432	            Per-slot alignment RMSD gate forwarded to build(); rejected
433	            structures are counted as errors, by default None
434	        min_distance : float or None, optional
435	            Post-build overlap gate forwarded to build(); structures
436	            with non-bonded atoms closer than this are counted as
437	            errors, by default None
438	        max_per_topology : int or None, optional
439	            Cap on the SBU combinations attempted per topology. The
440	            full product over slot types explodes combinatorially on
441	            multinodal nets; when it exceeds the cap, a seeded random
442	            sample of distinct combinations is built instead. -1 (or
443	            None, the default) disables the cap and enumerates
444	            exhaustively; the total combination count is logged before
445	            building starts so the cost is visible up front.
446	        seed : int or None, optional
447	            Seed for the sampling generator; a fixed seed makes the
448	            sampled enumeration reproducible.
449	        n_jobs : int, optional
450	            Number of worker processes; 1 (default) builds serially in
451	            this process. Builds are independent, so speedup is close
452	            to linear once workers are warm. On Windows and macOS the
453	            spawn start method re-imports the package (pymatgen
454	            included) in every worker, so a few seconds of warmup
455	            precede the first results.
456	        deduplicate : bool, optional
457	            Drop structurally equivalent duplicates from the result
458	            (different SBU combinations can converge to the same
459	            crystal). Matching uses pymatgen's StructureMatcher, keeps
460	            the first representative of each equivalence class, and is
461	            off by default: it is quadratic per composition group, and
462	            the raw enumeration is sometimes the point.
463	        checkpoint_dir : str, Path or None, optional
464	            Directory for on-disk checkpointing. Every finished
465	            combination is recorded there atomically (built frameworks
466	            as .json.gz, gate rejections as .failed markers); a rerun
467	            pointed at the same directory skips finished combinations
468	            and reloads their outcomes instead of rebuilding, so an
469	            interrupted enumeration resumes where it stopped. The
470	            ledger records outcomes, not settings - rerun with the
471	            same gates and seed. None (default) disables checkpointing.
472	
473	        Returns
474	        -------
475	        list[Framework]
476	            the frameworks produced by the building method
477	        """
478	        if max_per_topology is not None and max_per_topology < 1:
479	            if max_per_topology != -1:
480	                raise ValueError(
481	                    "max_per_topology must be a positive integer, or -1/None "
482	                    f"for no cap, got {max_per_topology}"
483	                )
484	            max_per_topology = None
485	        checkpoint = _Checkpoint(checkpoint_dir) if checkpoint_dir is not None else None
486	        logger.info("Building All Available Structures! This will take some time.")
487	        logger.info("============================================================")
488	        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
489	        frameworks: list[Framework] = []
490	        attempted = 0
491	        restored = 0
492	        # sieve pass first, so the full enumeration size is known (and
493	        # logged) before the first build starts: exhaustive runs can be
494	        # cost-estimated and aborted while still cheap
495	        plans: list[tuple[str, list[Fragment | int], list[list[str]]]] = []
496	        total = 0
497	        sampled = 0
498	        sieve_pbar = tqdm(self.list_topologies(subset=topology_subset))
499	        for topology_name in sieve_pbar:
500	            sieve_pbar.set_description(f"Sieving topology {topology_name:<5}")
501	            topology = self.topologies[topology_name]
502	            sbu_dict = self.list_building_units(
503	                sieve=topology_name, verbose=False, subset=sbu_subset
504	            )
505	            # slot types with no compatible SBU are absent from the
506	            # dict entirely, so completeness needs an explicit check
507	            if len(sbu_dict) != len(topology.mappings):
508	                continue
509	            if not all(sbu_dict.values()):
510	                continue
511	            slot_types = list(sbu_dict.keys())
512	            options = [sbu_dict[slot_type] for slot_type in slot_types]
513	            count = math.prod(len(choices) for choices in options)
514	            total += count
515	            if max_per_topology is not None and count > max_per_topology:
516	                sampled += 1
517	            plans.append((topology_name, slot_types, options))
518	        logger.info(
519	            f"\t[x] {total} SBU combinations over {len(plans)} buildable topologies."
520	        )
521	        if sampled:
522	            logger.info(
523	                f"\t[x] Sampling {sampled} topologies down to "
524	                f"{max_per_topology} combinations each."
525	            )
526	        executor = ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=n_jobs) if n_jobs > 1 else None
527	        # cap on submitted-but-unfinished chunks: bounds the validated
528	        # mappings (deep-copied fragments) alive at any moment
529	        max_pending = 2 * n_jobs
530	
531	        def finish(
532	            keys: list[str],
533	            results: list[Framework | None],
534	            i: int,
535	            framework: Framework | None,
536	        ) -> None:
537	            if checkpoint is not None:
538	                checkpoint.record(keys[i], framework)
539	            results[i] = framework
540	
541	        def drain(
542	            pending: deque[tuple[list[int], Future[list[Framework | None]]]],
543	            keys: list[str],
544	            results: list[Framework | None],
545	        ) -> None:
546	            indices, future = pending.popleft()
547	            for i, framework in zip(indices, future.result(), strict=True):
548	                finish(keys, results, i, framework)
549	
550	        try:
551	            topology_pbar = tqdm(plans)
552	            for topology_name, slot_types, options in topology_pbar:
553	                topology_pbar.set_description(f"Processing topology {topology_name:<5}")
554	                topology = self.topologies[topology_name]
555	                # combination name-tuples are cheap to hold; the heavy
556	                # deep-copied fragment mappings are produced lazily
557	                choices = list(_iter_combinations(options, max_per_topology, rng))
558	                attempted += len(choices)
559	                # per-topology results are indexed by choice so restored
560	                # and freshly built outcomes interleave in stable order
561	                results: list[Framework | None] = [None] * len(choices)
562	                keys: list[str] = []
563	                pending_idx = list(range(len(choices)))
564	                if checkpoint is not None:
565	                    keys = [checkpoint.key(topology_name, choice) for choice in choices]
566	                    pending_idx = []
567	                    for i, key in enumerate(keys):
568	                        if checkpoint.completed(key):
569	                            results[i] = checkpoint.load(key)
570	                            restored += 1
571	                        else:
572	                            pending_idx.append(i)
573	                validated_iter = (
574	                    (
575	                        i,
576	                        self._validate_mappings(
577	                            topology=topology,
578	                            mappings=dict(zip(slot_types, choices[i], strict=True)),
579	                        ),
580	                    )
581	                    for i in pending_idx
582	                )
583	
584	                if executor is None:
585	                    for i, mappings in validated_iter:
586	                        framework = _build_one(
587	                            topology, mappings, refine_cell, max_rmsd, min_distance
588	                        )
589	                        finish(keys, results, i, framework)
590	                else:
591	                    # chunked, windowed submission: the topology is
592	                    # pickled once per chunk (not per combination), and
593	                    # the FIFO window keeps ordering deterministic and
594	                    # memory flat
595	                    pending: deque[tuple[list[int], Future[list[Framework | None]]]] = (
596	                        deque()
597	                    )
598	                    for batch in _batched(validated_iter, BUILD_CHUNK_SIZE):

736	        """Validate and normalize the slot-to-fragment mappings.
737	
738	        Converts string SBU names to Fragment objects and ensures all
739	        topology slots have corresponding mappings.
740	
741	        Parameters
742	        ----------
743	        topology : Topology
744	            The topology blueprint being filled.
745	        mappings : dict[Fragment | int, Fragment | str]
746	            User-provided mappings from slot identifiers to SBU names or objects.

749	        -------
750	        dict[int, Fragment]
751	            Normalized mappings from slot indices to private Fragment
752	            copies. Neither the input dict nor the library fragments
753	            are aliased: alignment mutates fragments in place, and
754	            shared references would corrupt the SBU library.

756	        Raises
757	        ------
758	        ValueError

760	        """
761	
762	        def to_fragment(value: Fragment | str) -> Fragment:
763	            return self.sbu[value] if isinstance(value, str) else value
764	
765	        # slot-type keys first, so that index keys override them
766	        true_mappings: dict[int, Fragment] = {}
767	        for k, v in mappings.items():
768	            if not isinstance(k, int):
769	                if k not in topology.mappings:
770	                    valid = ", ".join(repr(s) for s in topology.mappings)
771	                    raise ValueError(
772	                        f"{k!r} is not a slot type of topology "
773	                        f"{topology.name!r}; its slot types are: {valid}. "
774	                        "Use the keys from list_building_units(sieve=...) "
775	                        "or plain slot indices."
776	                    )
777	                fragment = to_fragment(v)
778	                for i in topology.mappings[k]:
779	                    true_mappings[i] = fragment.copy()
780	        for k, v in mappings.items():
781	            if isinstance(k, int):

939	        Parameters
940	        ----------
941	        sieve : str or None, optional
942	            Name of a topology to filter SBUs by compatibility.

944	            sieve, all SBUs are returned grouped by connectivity

953	        dict[Fragment | int, list[str]]

955	            topology's representative slot Fragments); slot types with

957	            sieve: all SBU names keyed by connectivity (int).

978	            # connectivity instead (cheap: dummy counts only)

1	"""
2	Numpy alignment core for framework building.
3	
4	This module aligns SBUs onto topology slots and optimizes the cell,
5	replacing the earlier pymatgen-object pipeline. Two ideas drive it:
6	
7	1. **Directional matching.** Slot dummies sit at blueprint positions
8	   (quarter-edge points of a unit-scaled net) whose arm *lengths* carry
9	   no chemistry; only their *directions* do. SBUs are therefore matched
10	   to slots by optimally rotating their unit arm vectors onto the
11	   slot's unit arm vectors (Hungarian assignment + Kabsch, proper
12	   rotations only, so chiral SBUs are never silently mirrored).
13	
14	2. **Bond-length pair objective.** Every blueprint dummy site is
15	   shared by the two slots it connects (their tags coincide), and the
16	   built structure bonds the two SBU atoms that carried those dummies
17	   (the *anchors*). The correct cell is therefore the one where each
18	   paired anchor image sits one covalent bond length from its partner,
19	   and the optimization objective is the RMS deviation of the paired
20	   anchor distances from their Cordero covalent-radius targets - not
21	   the distance to blueprint positions, whose arbitrary arm lengths
22	   previously pulled cubic nets into anisotropic cells, and not dummy
23	   coincidence, which hard-codes whatever bond length the SBU library's
24	   dummy placement implies (0.7 A dummies = a 1.4 A bond for every
25	   element pair; MOF-5 came out at 12.77 A instead of ~12.9).
26	
27	Everything is precomputed once per build into plain numpy arrays: the
28	cell optimization loop runs no pymatgen construction and no deep
29	copies.

65	# Deterministic rotation multi-start for the direction matcher: the 24
66	# proper rotations of the cube spread well over SO(3) and are cheap.
67	_CUBE_ROTATIONS: np.ndarray = np.array(
68	    [
69	        m
70	        for m in (
71	            np.array(p, dtype=float) * np.array(s, dtype=float)
72	            for p in itertools.permutations(np.eye(3))
73	            for s in itertools.product((1.0, -1.0), repeat=3)
74	        )
75	        if np.isclose(np.linalg.det(m), 1.0)
76	    ]
77	)

79	# Iterations of the assignment <-> rotation refinement per start
80	_MATCH_ITERATIONS = 8

83	def kabsch(sources: np.ndarray, targets: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
84	    """Optimal proper rotation taking sources onto targets.
85	
86	    Parameters
87	    ----------
88	    sources, targets : np.ndarray
89	        (n, 3) paired coordinate sets, already centered.
90	
91	    Returns
92	    -------
93	    np.ndarray
94	        (3, 3) rotation matrix R with det(R) = +1 minimizing
95	        sum_i |targets[i] - R @ sources[i]|^2. The determinant
96	        constraint means chiral arrangements are never mirrored.
97	    """
98	    covariance = sources.T @ targets
99	    u, _, vt = np.linalg.svd(covariance)
100	    sign = np.sign(np.linalg.det(vt.T @ u.T))
101	    correction = np.diag([1.0, 1.0, sign])
102	    return np.asarray(vt.T @ correction @ u.T)
103	
104	
105	def match_directions(
106	    targets: np.ndarray, arms: np.ndarray
107	) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float]:
108	    """Match SBU arm directions onto slot dummy directions.
109	
110	    Runs a deterministic multi-start of alternating Hungarian
111	    assignment and Kabsch rotation, keeping the best result.
112	
113	    Parameters
114	    ----------
115	    targets : np.ndarray
116	        (n, 3) unit vectors of the slot dummy directions.
117	    arms : np.ndarray
118	        (n, 3) unit vectors of the SBU arm directions.
119	
120	    Returns
121	    -------
122	    tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float]
123	        - R: (3, 3) proper rotation such that R @ arms[perm[i]] aims
124	          at targets[i].
125	        - perm: (n,) arm index assigned to each target.
126	        - rmsd: root mean square residual between the matched unit
127	          vectors (dimensionless, 0 for a perfect shape match, up to
128	          2 for opposite directions).
129	    """
130	    n = len(targets)
131	    if len(arms) != n:
132	        raise AlignmentError(f"Cannot match {len(arms)} arms onto {n} slot dummies.")
133	    best: tuple[float, np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None
134	    for start in _CUBE_ROTATIONS:
135	        rotation = start
136	        # impossible assignment: never equal to a real permutation, so
137	        # the first iteration always refines
138	        perm = np.full(n, -1)
139	        for _ in range(_MATCH_ITERATIONS):
140	            rotated = arms @ rotation.T
141	            # cost = squared distance between unit vectors
142	            cost = -2.0 * (targets @ rotated.T)
143	            _, new_perm = linear_sum_assignment(cost)
144	            if np.array_equal(new_perm, perm):
145	                break
146	            perm = new_perm
147	            rotation = kabsch(arms[perm], targets)
148	        residual = targets - arms[perm] @ rotation.T
149	        score = float(np.sqrt((residual**2).sum(axis=1).mean()))
150	        if best is None or score < best[0]:
151	            best = (score, rotation, perm)
152	            if score < 1e-9:
153	                break
154	    if best is None:  # pragma: no cover - _CUBE_ROTATIONS is never empty
155	        raise AlignmentError("No rotation start produced a match.")
156	    score, rotation, perm = best
157	    return rotation, perm, score
158	
159	
160	def _unit(vectors: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
161	    """Row-normalize a (n, 3) array."""
162	    norms = np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)
163	    if np.any(norms < 1e-9):
164	        raise AlignmentError("Degenerate (zero-length) arm vector.")
165	    return np.asarray(vectors / norms)

168	# cell angles are clipped into this range during optimization to keep
169	# the lattice from collapsing into a degenerate matrix
170	_ANGLE_BOUNDS = (30.0, 150.0)

173	@dataclass(frozen=True)
174	class CellParametrization:
175	    """The free cell parameters allowed by a net's crystal system.
176	
177	    Optimizing all six lattice parameters independently can break the
178	    symmetry the net declares (a cubic net drifting to a != b != c).
179	    This class maps a reduced free-parameter vector onto the full
180	    (a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma), exposing exactly the degrees of
181	    freedom the crystal system allows: cubic 1, hexagonal/tetragonal/
182	    rhombohedral 2, orthorhombic 3, monoclinic 4 (unique angle freed),
183	    triclinic 6. Topologies without a spacegroup number fall back to
184	    free lengths with blueprint angles (the legacy behavior).
185	
186	    Layer nets (is_2d) get a layer mode instead: c is the slab padding,
187	    not a bonded direction - no dummy pair crosses it, the objective is
188	    flat in c and Nelder-Mead would drift - so **c stays exactly
189	    frozen** at the blueprint value. The free parameters come from the
190	    plane-group lattice family: hexagonal/square 1 (a), rectangular 2
191	    (a, b), oblique 3 (a, b, gamma).
192	    """
193	
194	    spacegroup_number: int | None
195	    blueprint_abc: tuple[float, float, float]
196	    blueprint_angles: tuple[float, float, float]
197	    is_2d: bool = False
198	
199	    @functools.cached_property
200	    def system(self) -> str:
201	        """Crystal system name derived from the spacegroup number."""
202	        number = self.spacegroup_number or 0
203	        if self.is_2d:
204	            # the stored number is the plane-group number (1-17); an
205	            # out-of-range or missing number gets the most general
206	            # layer family, which still keeps c frozen
207	            family = (
208	                plane_groups.layer_system(number) if 1 <= number <= 17 else "oblique"
209	            )
210	            return f"layer_{family}"
211	        if number >= 195:
212	            return "cubic"
213	        if number >= 143:
214	            hexagonal_axes = np.allclose(
215	                self.blueprint_angles, (90.0, 90.0, 120.0), atol=1e-3
216	            )
217	            return "hexagonal" if hexagonal_axes else "rhombohedral"
218	        if number >= 75:
219	            return "tetragonal"
220	        if number >= 16:
221	            return "orthorhombic"
222	        if number >= 3:
223	            return "monoclinic"
224	        if number >= 1:
225	            return "triclinic"
226	        return "unknown"
227	
228	    @functools.cached_property
229	    def _unique_angle_index(self) -> int:
230	        """Index of the monoclinic unique angle (largest |angle - 90|)."""
231	        deviations = np.abs(np.asarray(self.blueprint_angles) - 90.0)
232	        # default to beta when the blueprint is numerically orthogonal
233	        return int(np.argmax(deviations)) if deviations.max() > 1e-3 else 1
234	
235	    @property
236	    def n_free(self) -> int:
237	        return {
238	            "cubic": 1,
239	            "hexagonal": 2,
240	            "rhombohedral": 2,
241	            "tetragonal": 2,
242	            "orthorhombic": 3,
243	            "monoclinic": 4,
244	            "triclinic": 6,
245	            "unknown": 3,
246	            "layer_hexagonal": 1,
247	            "layer_square": 1,
248	            "layer_rectangular": 2,
249	            "layer_oblique": 3,
250	        }[self.system]
251	
252	    def expand(self, free: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, ...]:
253	        """Full (a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma) from the free parameters."""
254	        free = np.abs(np.asarray(free, dtype=float))
255	        system = self.system
256	        if system.startswith("layer_"):
257	            # c is the frozen slab padding, alpha = beta = 90 by
258	            # construction of the padded 2D lattice
259	            pad_c = self.blueprint_abc[2]
260	            if system == "layer_hexagonal":
261	                # 120 exactly: the plane-group operator tables assume
262	                # the standard hexagonal setting, and the blueprint
263	                # angle carries matrix-roundtrip noise
264	                (a,) = free
265	                return (a, a, pad_c, 90.0, 90.0, 120.0)
266	            if system == "layer_square":
267	                (a,) = free
268	                return (a, a, pad_c, 90.0, 90.0, 90.0)
269	            if system == "layer_rectangular":
270	                a, b = free
271	                return (a, b, pad_c, 90.0, 90.0, 90.0)
272	            a, b, gamma = free
273	            gamma = float(np.clip(gamma, *_ANGLE_BOUNDS))
274	            return (a, b, pad_c, 90.0, 90.0, gamma)
275	        if system == "cubic":
276	            (a,) = free
277	            return (a, a, a, 90.0, 90.0, 90.0)
278	        if system == "hexagonal":
279	            a, c = free
280	            return (a, a, c, 90.0, 90.0, 120.0)
281	        if system == "rhombohedral":
282	            a, alpha = free
283	            alpha = float(np.clip(alpha, *_ANGLE_BOUNDS))
284	            return (a, a, a, alpha, alpha, alpha)
285	        if system == "tetragonal":
286	            a, c = free
287	            return (a, a, c, 90.0, 90.0, 90.0)
288	        if system == "orthorhombic":
289	            a, b, c = free
290	            return (a, b, c, 90.0, 90.0, 90.0)
291	        if system == "monoclinic":
292	            a, b, c, unique = free
293	            angles = [90.0, 90.0, 90.0]
294	            angles[self._unique_angle_index] = float(np.clip(unique, *_ANGLE_BOUNDS))
295	            return (a, b, c, *angles)
296	        if system == "triclinic":
297	            a, b, c, alpha, beta, gamma = free
298	            alpha, beta, gamma = np.clip((alpha, beta, gamma), *_ANGLE_BOUNDS)
299	            return (a, b, c, float(alpha), float(beta), float(gamma))
300	        # unknown: free lengths, blueprint angles
301	        a, b, c = free
302	        return (a, b, c, *self.blueprint_angles)
303	
304	    def seed(self, abc_guess: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
305	        """Free parameters approximating an (a, b, c) length guess."""
306	        abc_guess = np.asarray(abc_guess, dtype=float)
307	        system = self.system
308	        if system in ("layer_hexagonal", "layer_square"):
309	            return np.array([abc_guess[:2].mean()])
310	        if system == "layer_rectangular":
311	            return abc_guess[:2].copy()
312	        if system == "layer_oblique":
313	            return np.array([*abc_guess[:2], self.blueprint_angles[2]])
314	        if system == "cubic":
315	            return np.array([abc_guess.mean()])
316	        if system in ("hexagonal", "tetragonal"):
317	            return np.array([abc_guess[:2].mean(), abc_guess[2]])
318	        if system == "rhombohedral":
319	            return np.array([abc_guess.mean(), self.blueprint_angles[0]])
320	        if system == "monoclinic":
321	            unique = self.blueprint_angles[self._unique_angle_index]
322	            return np.array([*abc_guess, unique])
323	        if system == "triclinic":
324	            return np.array([*abc_guess, *self.blueprint_angles])
325	        # orthorhombic and unknown
326	        return abc_guess.copy()

329	@dataclass
330	class SlotPlacement:
331	    """Precomputed geometry for one slot and its assigned SBU."""
332	
333	    slot_index: int
334	    frac_center: np.ndarray  # (3,) dummy centroid, fractional
335	    frac_arms: np.ndarray  # (n, 3) dummy positions minus center, fractional
336	    tags: list[int]  # (n,) blueprint tag per slot dummy
337	    sbu: Fragment
338	    arm_units: np.ndarray  # (n, 3) SBU unit arm vectors
339	    arm_lengths: np.ndarray  # (n,) SBU arm lengths, Angstrom
340	    sbu_center: np.ndarray  # (3,) SBU dummy centroid, cartesian
341	    dummy_indices: list[int]  # SBU atom index per arm
342	    # per arm: the anchor is the SBU atom bonded through that arm (the
343	    # dummy's nearest real atom); paired anchors bond in the output
344	    anchor_vecs: np.ndarray  # (n, 3) anchor positions minus center, cartesian
345	    anchor_radii: np.ndarray  # (n,) anchor covalent radii, Angstrom
346	    # per arm: unit anchor -> dummy direction in the SBU frame - the
347	    # bond direction the SBU's own chemistry wants (the dummy sits
348	    # along the bond), distinct from the centroid-based arm direction
349	    # for a bulky node
350	    bond_units: np.ndarray  # (n, 3)
351	    # arm assignment (perm) computed at the reference cell
352	    arm_for_target: np.ndarray
353	
354	    def rotation_for(self, matrix: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
355	        """Rotation and target directions in the given cell matrix."""
356	        directions = _unit(self.frac_arms @ matrix)
357	        ordered_arms = self.arm_units[self.arm_for_target]
358	        return kabsch(ordered_arms, directions), directions
359	
360	    def anchor_positions(self, matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
361	        """Cartesian SBU anchor positions (target order) in this cell."""
362	        rotation, _ = self.rotation_for(matrix)
363	        center = self.frac_center @ matrix
364	        ordered = self.anchor_vecs[self.arm_for_target]
365	        return np.asarray(center + ordered @ rotation.T)
366	
367	    def placed_geometry(
368	        self, matrix: np.ndarray, shift: np.ndarray | None = None
369	    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
370	        """Anchor positions and placed bond directions (target order).
371	
372	        ``shift`` is an optional fractional displacement of the slot
373	        centre (embedding relaxation); the SBU moves rigidly with its
374	        centre, so arms and rotation are unaffected.
375	        """
376	        rotation, _ = self.rotation_for(matrix)
377	        center = self.frac_center @ matrix
378	        if shift is not None:
379	            center = center + shift @ matrix
380	        anchors = center + self.anchor_vecs[self.arm_for_target] @ rotation.T
381	        directions = self.bond_units[self.arm_for_target] @ rotation.T
382	        return np.asarray(anchors), np.asarray(directions)
